findings.summary: Closing a directory-selected card returned focus to hidden content
findings.evidence: Visible directory summary is now the opener; all 21 locations and focus return pass.

findings.summary: Card choices consumed the detail region and minimum shell height clipped short viewports
findings.evidence: Nearby choices scroll with details; shell follows viewport height. Before screenshots and 320x568 / 844x390 regressions retained.

findings.summary: Pan/zoom dismissed the card and stole control focus
findings.evidence: Open-card native pan, zoom, Fit and Center now retain the card and expected control focus.

findings.summary: Nearby keyboard selection lost focus and changing location retained old scroll
findings.evidence: Nearby buttons retain focus; details reset on location change. The directory renders above an existing card so another location can be chosen.

findings.summary: Browser shortcuts were intercepted and Escape missed header/control focus
findings.evidence: Modifier keys pass through; Escape respects the topmost native modal and otherwise closes the card from map/header focus.

findings.summary: Unplotted card covered the normal desktop camera controls
findings.evidence: Unplotted cards open on the right, verified with actual hit-target bounds.

limitations: Chromium 156.0.8078.4 with fresh isolated Playwright processes/contexts. Physical phones, trackpads, Safari and Firefox were not tested.

Trusted browser wheel, mouse and emulated CDP touch were exercised. Line-mode wheel input and rate-tracker status/failure variants were simulated; the normal tracker and map use actual local handlers.
No screen reader was used. The focus ring and live-region/countdown structure were verified, but this is not a full accessibility certification.
A deliberately mocked HTTP 503 produces expected browser console/response entries in the recovery test. There were no unexpected browser errors.
This is scoped map/navigation QA, not gameplay-command QA, a security audit, deployment or production validation.
The independent reviewer examined the integration source at 777db30; the primary agent validated the later fixes. No independent final-code approval is claimed.
